paper.title: The SIMON and SPECK Families of Lightweight Block Ciphers

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Simon64/96, Simon64/128, Simon128/128, Simon128/192 and Simon128/256 encrypt the five appendix plaintexts to the five published ciphertexts (5 of 5 vectors)
decrypting each of those ciphertexts returns the plaintext (5 of 5 round trips)

expected_values_source.what: the five Simon known-answer vectors of the paper's appendix as transcribed in the Crypto++ test-vector file simon.txt (entries labelled "Appendix B (modified)"; the modification is byte reversal relative to the paper's printed word notation, undone when the tables were generated). The key-schedule constant sequences z2, z3, z4 (hexadecimal, bit i = z_i) come from the Crypto++ source file simon.cpp
expected_values_source.note: single transcription (the Linux kernel carries Speck but not Simon vectors); the paper PDF itself was not fetched (eprint 403). The z constants are data (constants of the cipher, copied as numbers); the five vectors exercise z2, z3 and z4 but not z0 and z1, so those two are not included. Vectors are data, no code was copied

negative_control: built with SIMON_FROT1=2 (f(x) = (S^2 x & S^8 x) ^ S^2 x), 0 of 5 vectors match and the program exits 1
not_checked: the Simon variants with 32-, 48- and 96-bit blocks (and z0, z1)
the Speck family (see the speck folder)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the five published Simon ciphertexts for their appendix inputs and inverts them. The vectors have one public transcription only. It does not show the cipher is secure.
